title: Albert-system clarinets and Willie Humphrey
summary: Gorman describes Albert-system clarinets and how Willie Humphrey struggled with his horn.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You're calling the Albert for the players who played Albert.
You say that the young Lorenzo Teo used Albert too.

Albert's system. And just here lately after the fellow just found out, let me see, I believe I was the only fellow I believe around here was using the Bernborn System home. Because as many times I used to catch a lot of them guys, you know, because we used to go in dances, at the time we used to give dances at that time, economy hall, corporators and stuff. And I'd catch them, I'd say, see, just like if you were Willie Umphrey. You know Willie Umphrey?

I'd say, oh Willie? I'd say, yeah, would you mind playing my players man for a couple of numbers? He'd say, all right, all right. He'd say, I'm going somewhere. Well I have my horn up there, he see the clarinet up there, you understand? Well I was going outside the horn and stand up maybe outside. And while the trumpet player said, come on, Willie, you going to play? He said, yeah. He'd come there and pick up the horn and feel it. He'd start to play, man he's done going back in short pants, you see. Just didn't understand it. And I done caught a lot of fellows like that. Well some of them used to ask me, man how you finger that horn? How you do this? Well I used to explain and tell them, see. And finally this fellow buy it, then the other fellow bought it, and that's how them horns come out. Because you take a clarinet player, if he wants to be a horn, or you know what I mean, want to be above him, if you had a bomb system clarinet, then nobody would want to take your place. Man, you've got that funny, come on man, I don't want to play, he just couldn't play. You see, because his position, you see he's used to that fork finger. Isn't that fork finger? And that B, when he hit that B with one finger. But you see with the bomb system you hit the B back here. You see it's opposite way. With the middle finger. That's right, you see it's opposite all the time, you see. But after you catch it, it's easy. But them fellows breathing that fork, you understand what I mean?
Playing all the wrong notes there.
